title: Clear costs
line: An honest total before the first appointment: estimator, side-by-side packages, add-ons with their HFEA ratings and ways to pay.
why: Tackles the clinic's worst public number (16 of 22 HFEA reviewers paid 'way above the estimate') and is the clearest route to more multi-cycle sales.
roi: Fewer drop-outs after consultation, more Duo and Multi-Cycle packages, a better HFEA patient rating.

title: Find your path
line: Entry points for each kind of patient, a quick eligibility check, and the journey from enquiry to the Rosie on one page.
why: The site is organised the way the clinic works, by service. Patients arrive as a couple, a single woman, a female couple, someone planning ahead or someone not eligible for NHS funding.
roi: Puts the most valuable self-funded visitors on the right price and next step in one or two clicks.

title: Start today
line: Enquire, book a call or an information session without leaving the page, at any hour, and measure every lead.
why: There is no form anywhere on the site. Every competitor checked captures enquiries on the page.
roi: The biggest single lever: more enquiries, captured out of hours, followed up faster, and finally counted.

title: Proof you can trust
line: Current success rates by age, real people, the team, the NHS difference and a plan to lift the HFEA patient rating.
why: Five-year-old charts, 2013 stories and a 2 out of 5 HFEA patient rating undersell a clinic with a 5 out of 5 inspection.
roi: Wins more of the people who shortlist on the HFEA site and compare Cambridge IVF with Bourn Hall.

title: Self-pay services hub
line: An egg freezing hub, online booking for private semen analysis, a donor pre-screen and online storage payments.
why: These are the services people pay for themselves, often without a referral, and the site currently treats them as footnotes.
roi: New self-funded revenue (egg freezing from £3,675 plus £346 a year storage) and faster collection of recurring fees.
